steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AO1: Demonstrate knowledge and understanding of geological ideas and methods (35%)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AO2: Apply knowledge and understanding of geology to familiar and unfamiliar contexts (35%)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: AO3: Analyse, interpret and evaluate geological information and methods (30%)

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Mathematical skills: calculating gradients, using standard form, ratios, percentages, interpreting graphs

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What is the difference between describe and explain? | Q: How should you approach a 6-mark extended writing question? | Q: What mathematical skills are required in GCSE Geology?

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Describe = state what you observe (facts, features, data). Explain = say why or how it happens (mechanism, cause, process). | 1) Identify the command word and focus. 2) Plan to cover all aspects. 3) Write in structured paragraphs with geological terminology. 4) Include specific examples or case studies. 5) If evaluating, con | Calculating gradients, using standard form, calculating ratios and percentages, interpreting data from tables and graphs, and calculating true thickness from apparent thickness and dip angle.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Command words: describe = what; explain = why/how; evaluate = weigh and conclude OCR J357 AO weightings: AO1 35%, AO2 35%, AO3 30% In maths questions: write formula, substitute, calculate, include units Fieldwork answers must use specific observations and correct terminology
